judge.rationale: The candidate's implementation in `chatOrchestrator.ts` is functionally identical to the reference, using a pure helper (`addUsage`) to accumulate per-round token counts while gracefully handling `undefined` usage on partial or all rounds. It satisfies every acceptance criterion in the ticket, notably testing a full two-tool-round turn (three provider calls) and an all-undefined turn, and making the hook signature unambiguous via both the parameter name (`turnUsage`) and a `TurnUsage` type alias with JSDoc. It also accurately updates `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the spec files with re-anchored line numbers. It scores 4 on closeness to reference because it exports a new `TurnUsage` type alias and scatters the new tests across three separate test files plus a shared `turnUsageTestSupport.ts` helper (requiring a `tsconfig.build.json` exclusion), whereas the reference simply renamed the parameter to `totalUsage` and added two tests directly into the existing `ChatOrchestrator tool loop` suite in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts`.
